description:
## Problem
On macOS 27.0.1 (arm64), `import chdb` fails in the BenchBox environment:
`ImportError: dlopen(.../chdb/_chdb.abi3.so): mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool, fileOffset=0x12369CAC`.
Installed chdb is 4.1.6; pyproject pins `chdb>=0.10.0` (core, clickhouse-local extra). Upstream chdb has released 4.2.1, 4.3.0 and 4.4.0. Reproduced 2026-11-12 (corpus reruns had to move to the benchbox-agent Linux machine) and again 2026-11-17. ClickHouse Local is therefore unusable for local development, UAT and measurement on the current macOS, and any Mac user on macOS 27 hits the same import error.

## Decision gate
1. PR #2719 (done item chdb-4x-native-load-and-old-engine-hang-20261005) showed chdb 4.4.0 with chdb-core 26.9.0 fails identically. The native library ships in chdb-core: test chdb 4.4.0 with the newest chdb-core (26.11.1 on 2026-11-17) and any newer chdb release. If one loads, raise the floor (uv add) and verify.
2. If none loads, this is an upstream defect: build a minimal reproducer (fresh venv, pip install chdb, import), record the upstream issue text for the owner to file, and make BenchBox report a clear, actionable error for clickhouse-local on affected macOS instead of a raw dlopen trace. Today the actionable message exists only in tests/utilities/optional_engines.py; the product import (benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/_dependencies.py import_chdb) raises the raw error. Do not file upstream without the owner.

## Guardrails
- Do not vendor or patch the binary.
- Do not mark ClickHouse Local unsupported on macOS without the owner.
- CI (Linux) results must not change; check the clickhouse-local test tier on Linux after any version change.
